Enthusiastic

/in-thoo-zee-AS-tik/ — stress on AS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is enthusiastic shows strong excitement and eager interest in something.

The enthusiastic volunteers arrived an hour early with homemade signs.

Worked Example

The new member raised her hand at every meeting, asked detailed questions, and stayed late to help set up the next event—everyone could see she was enthusiastic about joining the club.

enthusiast (one full of eager excitement) + -ic (having the characteristic of) = having the excited, eager energy of an enthusiast. Her repeated actions (raising hand, staying late) demonstrate the defining trait of someone passionate and engaged.

How Enthusiastic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

eager

eager: impatiently wanting to do or get something

keen

keen: strongly interested and quick to get involved

zealous

zealous: intensely devoted, almost to the point of fanaticism

Antonyms

apathetic

apathetic: showing no interest, energy, or emotion

indifferent

indifferent: not caring one way or the other

How Strong Is It? — willing → interested → eager → enthusiastic

willing vs. enthusiastic

willing vs. enthusiastic: A willing helper will do the job if you ask, but an enthusiastic one volunteers before you even finish asking.

interested vs. enthusiastic

interested vs. enthusiastic: She was interested enough to read one article about robotics, while her enthusiastic brother spent the summer building a robot in the garage.

eager vs. enthusiastic

eager vs. enthusiastic: An eager student raises a hand quickly, but an enthusiastic one stays after class begging for extra projects.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — enthusiast

Root — enthusiast: a person filled with eager excitement — built in two steps from enthusiasm (the feeling) to enthusiast (the person who feels it); ultimately from Greek enthous, 'possessed by a god' (en, 'in' + theos, 'god') (Greek)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of; having the nature of (Greek (via Latin -icus))

Put it together

Put it together: This word is built in a two-step chain: enthusiasm (eager excitement) names the feeling, an enthusiast is the person who feels it, and enthusiast + -ic = characteristic of an enthusiast. Deep inside sits Greek en + theos, 'a god within' — the ancient Greeks thought an enthusiastic person was literally inspired by a god.

Use the root in a new word: enthusiast

Use the root in a new word: enthusiast: My uncle is a model-train enthusiast who spends every weekend adding tiny buildings to his basement railway.

Word Building

Word Choice

positive/informal

Reach for enthusiastic when someone shows visible, energetic excitement and engaged interest — through actions, words, or body language. It's warmer and more openly expressive than synonyms like 'keen' and suggests genuine, infectious passion.
